Description.Summary: Mobile-Agent (v3) is an open-source, cross-platform GUI automation agent developed by Tongyi Lab at Alibaba Group. Its core is GUI-Owl — a foundational vision-language model built on Qwen2.5-VL — wrapped in a four-role multi-agent framework (Manager, Worker, Reflector, Notetaker) that automates tasks on Android phones, PCs, and web browsers without requiring app-specific training.

evidence.quote: GUI-Owl is a native end-to-end multimodal agent designed as a foundational model for GUI automation.

UI Agent is a multimodal agent solution that operates devices such as mobile phones, in-vehicle systems, TVs, and PCs based on screen understanding. It supports cross-application operations, requires no training, and is plug-and-play.

Practices.Summary: There is no conventional unit or integration test suite in the public repository. The repository contains no test discovery configuration. Quality assurance is done entirely through live agent runs against public benchmark environments.

evidence.quote: No releases published. No packages published.

Practices.Summary: Agent behaviour is validated by running the full agent stack against AndroidWorld and OSWorld interactive environments using shell scripts. These scripts launch live agent sessions against real or emulated devices and measure end-to-end task success rate. This is the closest equivalent to an integration test in the project.

evidence.quote: Run the evaluation. cd MobileAgent/Mobile-Agent-v3/os_world_v3 sh run_guiowl.sh sh run_ma3.sh

Practices.Summary: Community users act as de facto integration testers. With 185 open and 96 closed GitHub Issues, the majority of bug discovery happens through external researchers running the agent on their own devices and setups. The team relies on issue reports to surface runtime failures that would otherwise require live device testing.

evidence.quote: Open (185) Closed (96).

Tools.Summary: Testing tools are limited to: (1) shell scripts that drive evaluation runs; (2) AndroidWorld and OSWorld as live benchmark environments (installed separately); (3) the GUI-Critic-R1/test.py evaluation script using transformers, dashscope, and modelscope for inference

Others.Summary: The runtime code includes error-handling patterns: a 5-attempt retry loop for screenshot capture, try/except around JSON parsing with ast.literal_eval as fallback for Python-style dict outputs (introduced after PR #272), and RuntimeError raises for failed LLM API calls. These are guards against runtime failures, not test assertions.

Practices.Summary: The only automated GitHub Actions workflow is pages-build-deployment, which rebuilds the project's GitHub Pages static website on every push to main. As of May 2026 there have been 258 runs of this workflow. There are no CI workflows for running tests, linting code, building packages, or checking pull requests — all code integration is manual.

Tools.Summary: GitHub Actions (pages-build-deployment only) is the sole CI tool — used for website hosting, not code CI. Model artifacts are distributed via HuggingFace and ModelScope. The production API is served on Alibaba Cloud Bailian. The agent runtime uses ADB (Android Debug Bridge) for Android device control and pyautogui for desktop control. The Alibaba Cloud sandbox API (create_sandbox / kill_sandbox) isolates each cloud-based agent session.

evidence.quote: Alibaba's Mobile Use docs define an explicit sandbox lifecycle via create_sandbox and kill_sandbox, with sessions referenced by sandbox_id.

Stakeholders.Summary: The Tongyi Lab core team (approximately 22 GitHub contributors) manually manages releases and deployment. No dedicated DevOps or SRE role is publicly visible. Alibaba Cloud provides the compute platform for the Bailian API.

Issues.Issue_Title: Image size alignment mismatch in computer_use module causes coordinate offset
Issues.Summary: Community user identified that run_gui_owl_1_5_for_pc.py called smart_resize with factor=16 while utils.py used factor=28, introducing a ~1% coordinate error on desktop screenshots. Core maintainer junyangwang0410 pushed a direct commit referencing the issue and closed it the same day.

Issues.Issue_Title: Cannot Reproduce GUI-OWL-7B Results on AndroidWorld as Reported in Paper
Issues.Summary: User reported only ~20% task accuracy vs. 66.4% in the paper. Maintainer junyangwang0410 responded the same day with evaluation logs and trajectory files, pointing to a vLLM version incompatibility. Upgrading to the latest vLLM fully resolved the issue. Issue also cross-referenced in #238 (OSWorld reproduction), where upgrading from vLLM v0.8.0 to v0.11.0 fixed the same problem.
The _call_api function in the browser_use module raised a runtime error due to a missing API response field. Closed by core team after the fix was committed.

Issues.Issue_Title: GUI-Owl-1.5-32b-thinking model produces systematic coordinate offset
Issues.Summary: The thinking-variant of GUI-Owl-32B outputs click and swipe coordinates that are systematically off from the correct screen position. Remains open; no code fix or acknowledgment yet.

Issues.Issue_Title: parse_action raises IndexError when model output is empty or missing tool_call tag
Issues.Summary: When the model returns an empty string or a response without the expected tool_call wrapper, the action parser crashes with an IndexError instead of recovering gracefully. Remains open.

Issues.Issue_Title: Coordinate recognition inaccurate in Mobile-Agent-v3 (most discussed open issue)
Issues.Summary: The most-commented open issue (19 comments). Users report that the agent consistently clicks incorrect screen positions. Community has offered workarounds (e.g., toggling --coor_type flag) but the issue has not been closed by the core team.

Practices.Summary: The core team (primarily maintainer junyangwang0410) responds to issues on a best-effort basis with no formal SLA. For critical code bugs — where a community member provides a precise code-level diagnosis — the maintainer pushes a direct fix commit referencing the issue and closes it, often within one to two days. Issue #265 (smart_resize factor mismatch) followed this exact path: diagnosis in issue thread, commit pushed with 'Fix the bug in #265' message, issue closed the same day.

evidence.quote: junyangwang0410 added a commit that references this issue on Mar 24: Fix the bug in https://github.com/X-PLUG/MobileAgent/issues/265. junyangwang0410 closed this as completed on Mar 24.

Practices.Summary: For benchmark reproducibility issues — the second most common category — the resolution pattern is different. The maintainer responds with internal evaluation logs and trajectory files to help the user compare outputs. If the root cause turns out to be an outdated inference dependency (vLLM version), no code fix is applied; the reporter closes the issue themselves after upgrading their environment. Issues #203 and #238 both followed this path.

evidence.quote: Hi, here are our evaluation logs and trajectory. I compared the logs and found that the model outputs were quite different. Did you use the quantized version of GUI-Owl? Or did you deploy the GUI-Owl using vLLM? — junyangwang0410, Oct 10 2025.

Practices.Summary: Issues are not triaged with labels, milestones, or assignees. There is no visible prioritisation system: all issues sit in a single unlabelled queue. The 183 open vs. 67 closed ratio (73% open) reflects selective triage — issues get closed when either a code fix is committed or a reporter self-resolves. Architectural and recurring concerns (coordinate precision in #182, #278; context overflow in #266) remain open indefinitely because they have no single-commit fix.

evidence.quote: Labels: No labels. Assignees: No one assigned. Milestone: No milestone. Open (183) Closed (67).

Practices.Summary: Active community members provide first-line support for common setup and configuration questions, reducing the maintainer's response burden. In issue #238, community member BUPTyj posted a correct vLLM API parameter workaround before the core team responded. This peer-to-peer support in issue threads is the project's de facto help desk, filling the gap left by the absence of a documentation site or Discord channel.

Stakeholders.Summary: Bug reports come almost entirely from the open-source community — researchers and developers attempting to reproduce benchmark results or deploy the agent on their own devices. Others.Summary: The most persistent class of unresolved bugs is coordinate precision across all versions: #182 (19 comments, still open), #278 (coordinate offset in thinking model), and the historic #265 (smart_resize mismatch, now fixed). Each arises from the same root cause — the gap between the model's training resolution and the user's device resolution at runtime — but each version introduces a new variant. The --coor_type CLI flag introduced in v3 is the engineering mitigation, but issues continue to surface.

evidence.quote: 使用Mobile-Agent3坐标识别不准确 (Coordinate recognition inaccurate in Mobile-Agent3) — Issue #182, 19 comments, still open.

Practices.Summary: The team follows a research-gated, version-per-subdirectory development model. Each major iteration (v1 to v2 to Mobile-Agent-E to v3) is developed as a self-contained module in its own directory and released alongside an academic paper. Each release is triggered by a research milestone (paper acceptance or arXiv submission) rather than a sprint cycle or feature roadmap. Older version directories are kept intact to preserve reproducibility.

evidence.quote: Mobile-Agent-v3 (Preprint): Multi-modal and multi-platform GUI agent. Mobile-Agent-E (Preprint): Multi-agent for self-evolving mobile phone operation. Mobile-Agent-v2 (NeurIPS 2024): Multi-agent for multimodal mobile phone operation. Mobile-Agent-v1 (ICLR 2024 Workshop): Single-agent for multimodal mobile phone operation.

Practices.Summary: The team uses a TODO list inside the README to communicate planned upcoming releases to the community. Items like 'Open source evaluation code for GUI-Owl and Mobile-Agent-v3 on AndroidWorld' are listed and checked off as they are completed, serving as a lightweight public roadmap. This README-based TODO list is the only visible form of work tracking.

Stakeholders.Summary: The project is developed by approximately 22 GitHub contributors, all affiliated with Tongyi Lab at Alibaba Group.
